complex-note.text:
description: Kerotakis H2/O2 skeletal v1

note: {[author, date]: migration witness, nested: {count: .nan}}

references:
- >-
  Baulch, D. L., Bowman, C. T., Cobos, C. J., Cox, R. A., Just, Th., Kerr,
  J. A., Pilling, M. J., Stocker, D., Troe, J., Tsang, W., Walker, R. W.,
  Warnatz, J. "Evaluated Kinetic Data for Combustion Modeling. Supplement
  II." J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 34(3), 757-1397 (2005). DOI
  10.1063/1.1748524. Retrieved 2026-09-05.

units: {length: cm, quantity: mol, activation-energy: cal/mol}

phases:
- name: gas
  thermo: ideal-gas
  kinetics: gas
  species: [H2, O2, H2O, H, O, OH, HO2, H2O2, N2, Ar]

species:
- name: H2
  composition: {H: 2}
- name: O2
  composition: {O: 2}
- name: H2O
  composition: {H: 2, O: 1}
- name: H
  composition: {H: 1}
- name: O
  composition: {O: 1}
- name: OH
  composition: {O: 1, H: 1}
- name: HO2
  composition: {H: 1, O: 2}
- name: H2O2
  composition: {H: 2, O: 2}
- name: N2
  composition: {N: 2}
- name: Ar
  composition: {Ar: 1}

reactions:

# --- chain branching: the two steps that turn one radical into three ---
- equation: H + O2 => O + OH
  rate-constant: {A: 2.0656e+14, b: -0.097, Ea: 15023.26}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-branching-h-o2; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 895,
    summary Table 4.1 p. 780, preferred k = 3.43e-10 T^-0.097
    exp(-7560/T) cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.1 at
    800 K rising to +/- 0.2 at 3500 K; validity=800-3500 K;
    retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: O + H2 => OH + H
  rate-constant: {A: 3.8180e+12, b: 0.0, Ea: 7948.82}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-branching-o-h2-low; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 803, summary Table 4.1 p. 777, preferred k = [6.34e-12
    exp(-4000/T) + 1.46e-9 exp(-9650/T)] cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty
    delta log k +/- 0.2 over the whole range. The recommendation is a sum
    of two Arrhenius terms and is written here as two entries whose rates
    add, which is exactly what the sum means. This is the first term;
    validity=298-3300 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: O + H2 => OH + H
  rate-constant: {A: 8.7923e+14, b: 0.0, Ea: 19176.52}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-branching-o-h2-high; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 803, second Arrhenius term of the preferred k = [6.34e-12
    exp(-4000/T) + 1.46e-9 exp(-9650/T)] cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty
    delta log k +/- 0.2; validity=298-3300 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

# --- propagation: where the water actually comes from ---
- equation: OH + H2 => H2O + H
  rate-constant: {A: 2.1680e+8, b: 1.52, Ea: 3457.74}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-propagation-oh-h2; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 1029, summary Table 4.1 p. 782, preferred k = 3.6e-16 T^1.52
    exp(-1740/T) cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.1 at
    250 K rising to +/- 0.3 at 2500 K; validity=250-2500 K;
    retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: H + H2O => OH + H2
  rate-constant: {A: 4.5166e+8, b: 1.6, Ea: 17944.45}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-reverse-h-h2o; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 922,
    summary Table 4.1 p. 780, preferred k = 7.5e-16 T^1.6 exp(-9030/T)
    cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.2. This is the
    separately evaluated reverse of OH + H2 -> H2O + H. Both directions
    are carried as independent irreversible steps rather than derived
    from a thermochemical equilibrium constant, which is why the network
    can reach a steady state instead of running to completion;
    validity=800-2500 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: OH + OH => H2O + O
  rate-constant: {A: 3.3483e+4, b: 2.42, Ea: -1927.59}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-oh-oh; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 1032, summary
    Table 4.1 p. 782, preferred k = 5.56e-20 T^2.42 exp(970/T) cm3
    molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.15. The exponential is
    POSITIVE in the recommendation, so the activation energy written here
    is negative - a fitted parameter, not a barrier height. The same data
    sheet supplies the equilibrium constant for the reverse,
    O + H2O -> OH + OH, which the 2005 evaluation does not give a
    forward data sheet of its own and which this pack therefore omits;
    validity=250-2400 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

# --- the HO2 shunt: what stops a hydrogen flame below the crossover ---
- equation: H + O2 + M => HO2 + M
  type: three-body
  rate-constant: {A: 2.6474e+19, b: -1.3, Ea: 0.0}
  efficiencies: {Ar: 0.53, H2O: 11.5}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-shunt-h-o2-m; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 898
    with the preferred-values box on p. 900, summary Table 4.2 p. 797,
    preferred low-pressure limit k0(N2) = 7.3e-29 T^-1.3 cm6 molecule-2
    s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.1 at 298 K rising to +/- 0.2 at
    2000 K. N2 is the reference collider. The Ar and H2O efficiencies are
    the ratios of the same evaluation's k0(Ar) = 1.9e-29 T^-1.2 and
    k0(H2O) = 1.0e-28 T^-1.0 to k0(N2), evaluated at 1200 K - the three
    recommendations carry different temperature exponents, so a single
    efficiency number is an approximation and the temperature it was
    taken at is stated. The falloff to k_infinity is NOT modelled;
    validity=298-2000 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: H + HO2 => OH + OH
  rate-constant: {A: 4.4564e+14, b: 0.0, Ea: 1391.04}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-ho2-h-branch; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 919,
    summary Table 4.1 p. 780, preferred k = 7.4e-10 exp(-700/T) cm3
    molecule-1 s-1 for channel 2, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.15;
    validity=250-1000 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: H + HO2 => H2 + O2
  rate-constant: {A: 1.0539e+14, b: 0.0, Ea: 2046.82}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-ho2-h-terminate; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 919, summary Table 4.1 p. 780, preferred k = 1.75e-10
    exp(-1030/T) cm3 molecule-1 s-1 for channel 1, uncertainty delta
    log k +/- 0.3. The third channel, H + HO2 -> H2O + O, has a
    recommendation at 298 K only and no temperature dependence at all, so
    it is not carried here; validity=250-1000 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: OH + HO2 => H2O + O2
  rate-constant: {A: 9.2741e+15, b: 0.0, Ea: 17507.27}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-ho2-oh-terminate; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 1037, summary Table 4.1 p. 783, HIGH-TEMPERATURE preferred k =
    1.54e-8 exp(-8810/T) cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k
    +/- 0.5. The evaluation gives two disjoint expressions for this
    reaction, this one over 1300-2000 K and k = 4.8e-11 exp(250/T) over
    250-400 K, and NO RECOMMENDATION AT ALL between 400 and 1300 K.
    Anyone running this pack in that gap is interpolating on their own
    authority and should say so; validity=1300-2000 K;
    retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: HO2 + HO2 => H2O2 + O2
  rate-constant: {A: 4.2155e+14, b: 0.0, Ea: 11982.84}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-ho2-ho2-high; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 1109,
    summary Table 4.1 p. 784, first Arrhenius term of the preferred k =
    [7.0e-10 exp(-6030/T) + 2.2e-13 exp(820/T)] cm3 molecule-1 s-1,
    uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.15 over 550-800 K rising to +/- 0.4 at
    1250 K; validity=550-1250 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: HO2 + HO2 => H2O2 + O2
  rate-constant: {A: 1.3249e+11, b: 0.0, Ea: -1629.51}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-ho2-ho2-low; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 1109,
    second Arrhenius term of the preferred k = [7.0e-10 exp(-6030/T) +
    2.2e-13 exp(820/T)] cm3 molecule-1 s-1. The second term has a
    positive exponential and therefore a negative activation energy;
    validity=550-1250 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: H2O2 + M => OH + OH + M
  type: three-body
  rate-constant: {A: 1.2044e+17, b: 0.0, Ea: 45506.98}
  efficiencies: {Ar: 0.42}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-peroxide-split; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet p. 1036
    with the preferred-values box on p. 1037, summary Table 4.3 p. 800,
    preferred low-pressure limit k0(N2) = 2.0e-7 exp(-22900/T) cm3
    molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.2. N2 is the reference
    collider. The Ar efficiency is the ratio of the same evaluation's
    k0(Ar) = 3.8e-8 exp(-21960/T) to k0(N2), evaluated at 1200 K, the two
    barriers being different. The falloff to k_infinity = 3.0e14
    exp(-24400/T) s-1 is NOT modelled; validity=700-1500 K;
    retrieved=2026-09-05

# --- termination: where the radicals go to die ---
- equation: H + OH + M => H2O + M
  type: three-body
  rate-constant: {A: 2.2122e+22, b: -2.0, Ea: 0.0}
  efficiencies: {Ar: 0.38, H2O: 6.39}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-termination-h-oh-m; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 913, summary Table 4.2 p. 797, preferred low-pressure limit
    k0(N2) = 6.1e-26 T^-2.0 cm6 molecule-2 s-1, uncertainty delta log k
    +/- 0.5. N2 is the reference collider. The Ar and H2O efficiencies
    are the exact ratios of the same evaluation's k0(Ar) = 2.3e-26 T^-2.0
    and k0(H2O) = 3.9e-25 T^-2.0 to k0(N2) - all three carry the same
    temperature exponent, so these ratios are temperature independent;
    validity=300-3000 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

- equation: H + H + M => H2 + M
  type: three-body
  rate-constant: {A: 6.5279e+17, b: -1.0, Ea: 0.0}
  efficiencies: {H2: 2.65}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-termination-h-h-m; source=Baulch et al. 2005, data sheet
    p. 905, summary Table 4.2 p. 797, preferred low-pressure limit
    k0(Ar) = 1.8e-30 T^-1.0 cm6 molecule-2 s-1, uncertainty delta log k
    +/- 0.5. Argon is the reference collider because the evaluation gives
    no N2 value. The H2 efficiency is the ratio of the same evaluation's
    k0(H2) = 2.8e-31 T^-0.6 to k0(Ar) evaluated at 1200 K, the exponents
    being different; validity=200-2500 K; retrieved=2026-09-05

# --- initiation, for completeness, and far outside a bench flame ---
- equation: H2 + M => H + H + M
  type: three-body
  rate-constant: {A: 2.2282e+14, b: 0.0, Ea: 96081.33}
  efficiencies: {H2: 4.05}
  note: >-
    id=h2o2-initiation-h2-split; source=Baulch et al. 2005, summary
    Table 4.3 p. 800, preferred low-pressure limit k0(Ar) = 3.7e-10
    exp(-48350/T) cm3 molecule-1 s-1, uncertainty delta log k +/- 0.3.
    Argon is the reference collider. The H2 efficiency is the exact ratio
    of the same evaluation's k0(H2) = 1.5e-9 exp(-48350/T) to k0(Ar),
    both carrying the same barrier. This is the pack's only initiation
    channel and its evaluation starts at 2500 K, so at ordinary flame
    temperatures it contributes essentially nothing and the network must
    be given a radical source; validity=2500-8000 K; retrieved=2026-09-05
complex-note.mutation: Replace the entire existing root note with an ignored complex-key/nonfinite annotation; preserve every other byte.

custom-tag-invalid-composition.text:
description: tagged shape refusal
phases:
- name: gas
  thermo: ideal-gas
  species: all
species:
- name: A
  composition: !WrongComposition [1, 2]
- name: B
  composition: {H: 2}
reactions:
- equation: A => B
  rate-constant: {A: 1.0, b: 0.0, Ea: 0.0}

scope: Source-informed parser/CLI engineering controls: exactly fifteen individual invocations, eleven expected successes and four expected refusals.
limits: No empirical rate constants, reaction yields, ignition delay, flame properties or solver accuracy are forecast.
Pack files carry their own Kerotakis CC BY 4.0 provenance; the collector does not redistribute third-party mechanism files.
1500 K is a mechanical migration input, not a statement that all published per-reaction validity ranges overlap or apply there.
The inert-only short trajectory deliberately avoids stiff combustion and does not establish active integration fidelity.
Binary SHA is independently required; exact compilation/source/lock provenance must be supplied and reviewed separately.
Frozen expectations and all failures must be preserved; an observed baseline failure does not authorize rewriting forecasts.
pack_attribution: Kerotakis gas-phase mechanism packs, CC BY 4.0; derived complex-note witness retains the same attribution.
